title: The recall list skipped everyone who never had an exam

data.workspace: recall.sql, the annual diabetic eye exam recall, Valley Bend Community Health Center (fictional)

flags.label: Quality manager, Rosa Delgado
flags.text: The recall list has 1,180 patients, but our registry shows about 1,900 adults with diabetes overdue. Letters print at 14:00.

flags.label: Pattern
flags.text: No patient on the list has never had an eye exam.

flags.label: Letters
flags.text: 14:00: recall letters printed from the list as it stood.

lines.text: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM patients p JOIN problems d ON d.patient_id = p.id AND d.code = 'DIABETES'
LEFT JOIN eye_exams e ON e.patient_id = p.id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM eye_exams e WHERE e.patient_id = p.id AND e.exam_date >= current_date - interval '12 months');
LEFT JOIN eye_exams e ON e.patient_id = p.id
WHERE e.exam_date < current_date - interval '12 months' OR e.exam_date IS NULL;
JOIN eye_exams e ON e.patient_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id HAVING max(e.exam_date) < current_date - interval '12 months';

objective: Relational databases, data modelling and SQL: tables linked by primary and foreign keys, and queries that join them to pull data on many patients
secondaryObjectives: Analyzing, reporting and visualizing data so it supports a decision

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. EXISTS: 'If it returns at least one row, the result of EXISTS is true; if the subquery returns no rows, the result of EXISTS is false'; 'The subquery can refer to variables from the surrounding query'; a correlated EXISTS 'is like an inner join ... but it produces at most one output row for each tab1 row, even if there are several matching tab2 rows'. NOT EXISTS is its negation (author's statement).

brief.situation: You maintain recall.sql at Valley Bend Community Health Center (fictional). It lists adult patients with diabetes who have had no eye exam in the past 12 months, for recall letters. The list has 1,180 patients; the registry suggests about 1,900. Letters print at 14:00. It is 13:05. All patients are invented test records; the query runs on a de-identified test copy first.
handover: patients(id, ...), problems(patient_id, code), eye_exams(patient_id, exam_date): one row per exam; a patient can have none or many.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look, change, check or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the quality manager: why patients were missing, what you changed, and how you know.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: eye_exams is linked to patients by a foreign key, one row per exam; a LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched patients with NULLs, but a WHERE on e.exam_date discards them; joining also matches a patient's old exam even when a recent one exists.
parts.modelAnswer: WHERE on the outer table dropped NULLs.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: NOT EXISTS an exam within 12 months, one row per patient whatever the exam count; OR IS NULL still recalls the recently examined; an inner join drops the never-examined.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: Counts reconcile with the registry and a 40-chart spot-check on the test copy.

scoring.modelReasoning: A recall list with no never-examined patients means the query drops patients without exam rows. The LEFT JOIN keeps them with NULL exam dates, and then WHERE e.exam_date < cutoff throws them away; it also matches a patient's old exam when a recent one exists. The question is about absence: NOT EXISTS an exam in the last 12 months, one row per patient. OR IS NULL still recalls the recently examined; an inner join drops the never-examined. Reconcile with the registry and spot-check charts on the test copy.
